profile.population_rule: Combat-unit people physically available in the engagement area before first hostile contact; excludes absent, hospitalized, noncombatant, detached and subsequent-arrival populations.
profile.boundary_rule: Same boundary and target-population definition for both sides; source-supported relative ordering allowed, no fabricated clock precision.

boundaries.contact_definition: Proposed B0: immediately before the first hostile contact of the April 6 assault, including reconnaissance and picket contact. Beauregard p386 nominates a reconnaissance/advance-picket encounter before the general advance; its 5 a.m. is an attributed clock, not an adjudicated exact boundary. Whether this is the earliest qualifying contact remains unestablished.
boundaries.availability_rule: Proposed rule for both sides: combat-unit people physically present in the final mapped engagement area at B0, including officers, artillery crews, cavalry, reserves and outposts. Later action, a front-line position, equipment quality and a readiness score are not membership criteria. Exclude noncombatant duties, absent/hospitalized personnel, out-of-area detachments and subsequent arrivals. Transport/afloat and perimeter cases remain unresolved; no complete membership partition is supplied.

boundaries.rationale: A non-releasing boundary proposal, not proof of earliest contact or a complete area. Pittsburg west-bank camps, landing, immediate attack approaches, reserves, pickets and ford guards are the proposed mapping task. Crump's Landing, Savannah and the opposite bank are outside that proposed local area. Exact outer perimeter, afloat treatment, first-contact identification and both side membership lists remain unresolved. No time zone, replacement time, combat readiness or zero-strength inference is made. See docs/research/shiloh-opening-boundary-v1.md and the bound research record.
